objective: For each reachable support row r and forced root pair q, accumulate Phi(r,q)=sum_x(C[q](x)-f(x))^2 over all primary inputs belonging to r. Count each primary input exactly once.
architecture: For each shared five-input row t, variables A(t),B(t) determine O5=B(t) and O6=I5?A(t):B(t). Orientation and selector are fixed to the incumbent; variable identifications use its actual half-table support masks.
hard_constraint: For every grouped row and half-table assignment, retain the maximum absolute error across all primary inputs. Assign forbidden choices penalty M=1+sum_t(max_q Phi(t,q)); every feasible assignment has total cost strictly below M.
reduction: Aggregate factors between the same pair of Boolean variables. A consistent polarity assignment making E01+E10-E00-E11 nonnegative permits the standard binary submodular graph-cut construction. Inconsistent polarity cycles return NON_ORIENTABLE and retain the incumbent.
exactness: The mincut is an exact SSE minimizer only for the supplied fixed topology, support masks, numeric cost table and orientable class. It is not a global placed-circuit optimum, does not solve arbitrary weighted2SAT, and does not imply polynomial whole-flow complexity.
implementation_guard: Incumbent support consistency and hard feasibility are checked. The returned assignment is checked against every hard row. Incumbent table SSE must equal the preceding independently evaluated circuit SSE. Each accepted replacement must reproduce the predicted integer SSE on a separate complete-domain replay.
acceptance: Strictly smaller SSE; unchanged WCE budget; no larger structural proxy tuple; retain original method otherwise. Actual area and timing are evaluated after synthesis and routing, even when support is unchanged.
scalability: R21 still enumerates all2^24inputs to construct numeric contexts. The small mincut solve does not remove this exponential context-generation limit.
novelty_boundary: Graph-cut optimization, polarity transformations, error compensation and squared-error objectives are established tools. Any publishable increment must come from the specific hardware-constrained numerical construction and measured advantages over the declared controls.
